subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph
notes:
PB55 FOLD (2026-10-15, owner decision 2026-08-08 'THE RULE IS THE UNIT'): the transcription printed this rule's nested list(s) at column 0, so 10 sub-item(s) held rows of their own; indented at their measured printed level, they are this rule's body and their adjudications are folded here, nothing dropped.

[the rule's own record before the fold]
kb/Work PB976 (2026-09-22): the CLASS clause's FOR phrase was PARSED AND IGNORED, so SR17's class-dependent half went unenforced and this row was CONFORMS on evidence that never exercised it. SwitchBindClass now reads the phrase once (ForPhraseIsNational — a) ALPHANUMERIC implied) and enforces b1/c1 (the IN alphabet's class), b2/c2 (unsigned, and within the native set or alphabet-name-4's), b3/c3 (each noninteger literal's class — the classifier had also let N"..." pass as alphanumeric), b4/c4 (one character under THROUGH — literal-6 used to be dropped silently) and b5/c5 (the count against alphabet-name-4's set; unreachable without IN) through the ONE operand decoder the ALPHABET clause uses, under SR17's own item numbers (COBOL1671); d) is the ONE resolver's (COBOL1669). One positive per class in the 2002 golden, one negative per arm in ClassClauseForPhraseTests. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Switches.cs#LiteralChars (kb/Work PB976: the CLASS clause's private operand decoder (LiteralChars, later ClassLiteralChars) is deleted; its operands now go through the ONE SPECIAL-NAMES decoder LiteralPhraseOperand, named above)

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L6.1 = §12.3.7.3 17) b) 1.: CONFORMS]
SR17 b)1 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'When the IN phrase is specified, alphabet-name-4 shall reference an alphabet that defines an alphanumeric character set.' -> OK 17) 1.). SwitchBindClass reads the FOR phrase once (ForPhraseIsNational, with SR17 a implying ALPHANUMERIC), resolves IN through CodedCharacterSetOf, and refuses `inSet.National != national` with COBOL1671 'SR17 b1'. The test rows PB976B1 (implied) and PB976B1F (explicit FOR ALPHANUMERIC) pin the message, and PB976OKAF/PB976OKNI are the positive controls. A LOCALE or undeclared alphabet-name-4 is refused by the resolver before the class test (CA5 -> COBOL1669). [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (base clause present at every edition; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change) (the IN phrase's own introduction edition is not stated by the 2023 text; see dossier_gaps)]

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L6.2 = §12.3.7.3 17) b) 2.: CONFORMS]
kb/Work PB1091: SR17 b)2 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'Literal-5, if numeric, shall be an unsigned integer and shall have a value within the range of one through the maximum number of characters in the native alphanumeric character set' -> OK 17) 2.). Both halves at every magnitude through the one ordinal reader: +65 -> 'unsigned', 129 IN STANDARD-1 and 99999999999 (with or without IN) -> the range rule, never the noninteger-literal rule SR17 b3.

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L6.3 = §12.3.7.3 17) b) 3.: CONFORMS]
SR17 b)3 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'Each noninteger literal shall be an alphanumeric literal.' -> OK, resolving to the identical SR14 b)2 sentence in the same clause 12.3.7.3). Probes: CA12 (B"1", boolean) and CA4 (1.5, noninteger numeric) -> COBOL1671 'SR17 b3'. The PB976B3 test (N"0" THRU N"9") pins the national literal. X"41" is alphanumeric (§8.3.3.2 hex format) and is accepted, which is correct. ALL literal operands are class-checked per operand (AllLiteralCharacters). The mislabel of an over-Int32 INTEGER as 'noninteger' belongs to b2's edge (L6.2), not to this rule, since every true noninteger literal is classified correctly. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (base clause present at every edition; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change)]

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L6.4 = §12.3.7.3 17) b) 4.: CONFORMS]
SR17 b)4 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'Each alphanumeric literal, when a THROUGH phrase is specified, shall be one character in length.' -> OK 17) 4.). SwitchBindClass runs OneCharacterOperands([lo, hi]) on both THROUGH operands after decoding. The PB976B4 test ("AB" THRU "C") pins the COBOL1671 message. CA15 (`"A" & "B" THRU "C"`, a concatenation folded to 'AB') -> 'SR17 b4'. CA16 (`ALL "A" THRU "C"`, one character per §8.3.3.6.4 GR3 c) is accepted and runs correctly. Without THROUGH a multi-character literal is legal and contributes each of its characters (GR12 b). [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (base clause present at every edition; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change)]

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L6.5 = §12.3.7.3 17) b) 5.: CONFORMS]
SR17 b)5 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'The number of characters specified shall not exceed the number of characters in the native alphanumeric character set or, when the IN phrase is specified, the number of characters in the character set referenced by alphabet-name-4.' -> OK 17) 5.). Under IN, SwitchBindClass compares the distinct member count with inSet.OrdinalCount. The test pins 256 > 128 for STANDARD-1, and CA11 (`1 THRU 128 "A" IN STD`: 128 distinct characters, since 'A' is ordinal 66 of STANDARD-1) is accepted and runs. The native half cannot be violated, because the members are distinct characters of the 65,536-character repertoire; the code comment says so and the reasoning holds. Counting distinct characters, not specifications, is the reading 'number of characters' supports. The trailing fragment 'c) When the NATIONAL phrase is specified:' is a heading, decided under L7.x. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (base clause present at every edition; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change)]

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L7.1 = §12.3.7.3 17) c) 1.: CONFORMS]
SR17 c)1 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'When the IN phrase is specified, alphabet-name-4 shall reference an alphabet that defines a national character set.' -> OK 17) 1.). This is the same `inSet.National != national` test as b1, keyed on the FOR NATIONAL reading. The PB976C1 test row (`CLASS C2 FOR NATIONAL IS 1 THRU 5 IN AA`) pins COBOL1671 'SR17 c1', and PB976OKNI (`CLASS C2 NATIONAL IS 946 THRU 970 IN NA`) is the positive control. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the NATIONAL phrase and the national character set enter at 2002; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change)]

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L7.2 = §12.3.7.3 17) c) 2.: CONFORMS]
kb/Work PB1091: SR17 c)2 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'Literal-5, if numeric, shall be an unsigned integer and shall have a value within the range of one through the number of characters in the native national character set' -> OK 17) 2.). The national arm and its IN arm (CharAt against the IN set, UCS-4: 1,112,064 characters) read the ordinal through the one reader at every magnitude.

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L7.3 = §12.3.7.3 17) c) 3.: CONFORMS]
SR17 c)3 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'Each noninteger literal shall be a national literal.' -> OK, the identical SR14 c)2 sentence in clause 12.3.7.3). The PB976C3 test ("0" THRU "9" in a FOR NATIONAL class) and PB976C3A (ALL "AB") pin COBOL1671. CA13 (X"41", an alphanumeric hex literal) -> 'SR17 c3'. CA14 (NX"0041" THRU N"C") is accepted and runs correctly, because NX is a national hex literal (§8.3.3.5). A figurative constant is a character per GR10, not a class violation. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the NATIONAL phrase and the national character set enter at 2002; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change)]

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L7.4 = §12.3.7.3 17) c) 4.: CONFORMS]
kb/Work PB1091: SR17 c)4 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'Each national literal, when a THROUGH phrase is specified, shall be one character in length.' -> OK 17) 4.). The one-character test is asked of the operand AS WRITTEN (PhraseOperand.IsOrdinal): a national LITERAL of other than one character is refused under c4 (N"A" THRU N"YZ"), a NUMERIC ordinal is no national literal and is held to c2 instead, so a BMP ordinal range under IN UCS-4 is accepted. A numeric ordinal that names a SUPPLEMENTARY character (two UTF-16 code units) has no position in the native-set run GR12 expands for a THROUGH phrase; the specification is silent on that pair, so it is refused under its own message naming GR12 (implementor-defined, docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-188), never under c4.

[folded SR-12.3.7.3-L7.5 = §12.3.7.3 17) c) 5.: CONFORMS]
Two rules in one row. (1) SR17 c)5 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'The number of characters specified shall not exceed the number of characters in the native national character set or, when the IN phrase is specified, the number of characters in the character set referenced by alphabet-name-4.' -> OK 17) 5.). The code path is shared with b5: the distinct count is checked against inSet.OrdinalCount under IN. Every national IN set (NATIVE/UTF-16 65,536; UCS-4/UTF-8 1,112,064; a literal-phrase national alphabet, which contains every native character) is at least as large as the 65,536-character native repertoire that members are drawn from, and no national code-name exists (PB793). So c5 cannot be violated by any source, and the check is correctly unconditional on class. (2) SR17 d) (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'Alphabet-name-4 shall not reference an alphabet specified with the LOCALE phrase.' -> OK 17) d)) goes through CodedCharacterSetOf. CA5 (alphanumeric LOCALE alphabet) and CA6 (FOR NATIONAL LOCALE alphabet) -> COBOL1669 citing 'SR17 d'. No test targets SR17 d or c5 (grep 'SR17 d' in tests: none; the symbolic twin is pb110-symbolic-locale-alphabet), so test-ref is empty. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the NATIONAL phrase and the national character set enter at 2002; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change); d) (the LOCALE phrase) likewise 2002+]
